_comment: Where a generated component deliberately does not draw what upstream draws,
named by the slot the two disagree on and by the reason.
Every other slot on the same page still gates at zero. This is not a
tolerance: it is the list of decisions this pipeline has made against its
own source, each one written down where the check would otherwise report it
every run and teach nobody anything.
A slot listed here that no longer differs FAILS the run: the decision was
reversed, or upstream moved, and either way the list is wrong. A slot that
differs and is not listed fails as it always did.
Adding one is a decision, not a fix. The question to answer first is
whether the difference is the reader misreading upstream — which is what
this check exists to find, and what it has found every other time.

plan.default.why: AI Elements writes `asChild` and this shadcn build is Base UI, whose equivalent is `render`. So `<Collapsible asChild><Card>` and `<CollapsibleTrigger asChild><Button>` each draw two elements upstream, and the second of those is a <button> inside a <button> — which axe reports as nested-interactive and is right to. The reader takes `asChild` at its word and draws one element, so the card is the collapsible and the trigger is the button.

mic-selector.default.why: Two of a kind. `<PopoverTrigger asChild><Button>` is the same `asChild` that `plan.default` records — a no-op in a Base UI build, so upstream draws a button inside its trigger and the reader draws one element. And the command palette this component folds is drawn closed here and not drawn at all there: upstream reads the device list from `navigator.mediaDevices`, which reports nothing without a permission prompt, so React renders an empty list and unmounts it.

chain-of-thought.default.why: Upstream renders two `<Collapsible>` wrappers — one around the header and one around the content — and threads the open state between them through a React context. The disclosure recipe folds a component into one function precisely because its parts have to agree about one id, so there is one collapsible here and the 16px `space-y-4` between the two of upstream's has nothing to sit between.

queue.default.why: The same scroll area as `suggestion.default`, folded as markup with its recipe left behind: Base UI unmounts a scrollbar with nothing to scroll and measures the viewport with a hook, and neither travels with a copy. A fold that carries a hook-owning recipe is the half of phase 3 that was recorded rather than built — see PLAN.md.

suggestion.default.why: The scroll area is folded as markup and its recipe stays behind: Base UI unmounts a scrollbar with nothing to scroll and measures the viewport with a hook, and neither travels with a copy. A fold that carries a hook-owning recipe is the half of phase 3 that was recorded rather than built — see PLAN.md.
